newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on correction.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Wednesday on a technical correction after sharp rises over the past few trading days, traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,250 yuan ($2,823) per tonne, losing 150 yuan. It opened down at 23,200 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,290 and a low of 23,180.
March fell 90 yuan to 23,080, April 200 to 23,090, May 130 to 23,260, July and August 150 to 23,250.
Combined volume fell to 41,310 tonnes from 47,290.
Copper opened lower and consolidated around low levels for most of the session.
"A technical correction is the main factor for today's falls, but follow-up selling is limited, with investors still optimistic over the mid-term market trend," said one trader.
"Copper is likely to fall in the next few days," another trader said. "But the downward potential is limited due to support from the high spot price."
Spot copper is currently above 22,500 yuan per tonne.
Aluminium ended mostly down. The March 1997 contract did not trade. April fell 50 yuan to 16,000 per tonne and May 40 to 16,340. Combined volume fell to 1,580 tonnes from 3,460.
